translation:
Target is the proposition that for every set of formulas T (with no additional restrictions on T), if T proves the closed formula ∃ x₁, ∀ x₀, (K (¬ R₀(x₀, x₀)) ↔ R₀(x₁, x₀)), then T also proves the closed formula ∃ x₁, (¬ R₀(x₁, x₁)) ∧ (¬ K (¬ R₀(x₁, x₁))).

Here the formal language consists of formulas built from binary atomic formulas R_r(a, b) (atom r a b, with relation index r ∈ ℕ and variable arguments a, b ∈ ℕ; in Target, R₀ denotes relation index 0 and x₀, x₁ denote variables 0 and 1), falsity (fls), implication (→), universal quantification over natural-number variables (∀ x), and a unary operator K, with ¬ φ defined as φ → fls, φ ∧ ψ as ¬(φ → ¬ψ), φ ↔ ψ as (φ → ψ) ∧ (ψ → φ), and ∃ x, φ as ¬ ∀ x, ¬ φ.

Provability from T is defined inductively using only modus ponens (from φ → ψ and φ, infer ψ), hypotheses from T, and an axiom set consisting of (a) all universal generalizations (zero or more applications of ∀ x) of the basic axioms listed below, together with (b) all formulas of the form K ψ where ψ is such a universal generalization of a basic axiom (note that neither a general rule of universal generalization nor a general rule of necessitation is included as a primitive rule on derivations from T, and in the axiom set K is applied at most once directly to universally generalized basic axioms). The eight basic axiom schemas are: (1) all propositional tautologies (formulas satisfied by every valuation v : Form → Prop with ¬ v(fls) and v(φ → ψ) ↔ (v(φ) → v(ψ))); (2) universal instantiation (∀ x, φ) → φ[y/x] whenever y is free for x in φ (substituting y for free occurrences of x without variable capture); (3) quantifier distribution (∀ x, (φ → ψ)) → ((∀ x, φ) → (∀ x, ψ)); (4) vacuous quantification φ → (∀ x, φ) when x does not occur free in φ; (5) K (φ → ψ) → (K φ → K ψ); (6) K φ → φ; (7) K φ → K (K φ); and (8) K (∀ x, φ) → ∀ x, (K φ).

divergences.description: In Reinhardt's Theorem 3 [P-R326], U(e, x) is any formula with two free variables, whereas Target hardcodes U to a single fixed atomic binary relation symbol (Def15, i.e., atom 0). Even within Form, Target does not quantify over arbitrary formulas with two free variables (nor over relation indices), thereby treating U schematically and bypassing variable-capture/renaming issues for compound formulas.

Reinhardt's setting [P-R323, P-R326] is the language and axiomatic theory of arithmetic (with constants, function symbols, equality, and arithmetic axioms plus B applied to them) extended with B, which enables the Post-Turing thesis instance where U is an r.e. universal formula. The Lean context is a purely relational first-order modal fragment without function symbols, constants, equality, or arithmetic (with T ranging over arbitrary sets of formulas in Form); this is an idealization (acknowledged by the author) that suffices for the logical core since the argument uses only first-order logic and Bp → p.

Theorem 3 [P-R326] assumes a) universally for every formula p(x) with one free variable and concludes existentially that there is some formula q(e) satisfying b). Target instead assumes a) only for the single instance p(x) := ¬U(x, x) and establishes b) for the explicit witness q(e) := ¬U(e, e). For a fixed U, this is a harmless strengthening (weaker antecedent, stronger consequent) that matches the specific instantiation used in Reinhardt's proof.

In [P-R323], Reinhardt adopts the universal closures (sentences) of the axiom schemas, optionally prefixed by B, whereas Def12 and Def13 in Lean include arbitrary (possibly partial or empty) universal generalizations of the schemas and K ψ for open ψ. Given the Barcan-converse axiom kall (K(∀x φ) → ∀x K φ) and universal instantiation, this generates the same provable formulas and is a harmless presentational difference.

judgement.summary: Target accurately formalizes the logical deduction from a) to b) in Reinhardt's Theorem 3 (including quantification into the modal operator K and Reinhardt's four modal axiom schemas) for the proof's diagonal instance p(x) := ¬U(x, x), q(e) := ¬U(e, e). The divergences are minor idealizations and weakenings/strengthenings—chiefly fixing U to a single atomic binary relation symbol in a pure first-order modal fragment lacking arithmetic and equality, specializing p and q to the proof's witness, and allowing open generalizations in the axiom set.
